failures.feature: Hide answers (row 14) → SR3 Second look: keeping keys hidden until the student has re-tried each miss
failures.why_not_way_better: Not buildable as written. The results payload only drops four fields for misses the student hasn't seen: answer, reasons, rationale and mistake. Several other fields added in the same file still give the key away: crowd.option_share is null at the key, accepted lists the key's accepted grid-in forms, and the SR10 diagnosis says things like 'Right value, too few digits: 2/3 needs .6666' or 'Right size, wrong sign'. P1's steps, diverge and option_steps also leak it, since the last step's value equals the key. So do the SR8 cause evidence 'you crossed out the answer' and SR9's judgement.crossed_key chips, which mark the key and open it struck. CSV, print, the tutor packet and the repair pack all print the key, and nothing says what they do while a second look is still offered. Acceptance check 1 only tests for a missing `answer` field, so these leaks pass. The one feature that makes this row better than theirs doesn't hold.
failures.fix: Define the held-back set as every field derived from the key: answer, reasons, rationale, mistake, steps, diverge, option_steps, accepted, diagnosis, crowd.option_share, cause.evidence lines about the key, crossed_key entries, and struck marks on the key. While the offer stands, CSV and print show 'Hidden' for these questions, or ask first ('This shows the answers and ends your second look') and then set seen_key. Acceptance: for every unseen miss, a jq check finds none of those fields, and judgement.crossed_key contains no unseen qid.

failures.feature: Domain performance and their hidden domainScore (rows 7–8) → SR1 '≈ −55 pts · 40% of your gap' and the weight check
failures.why_not_way_better: The spec contradicts itself. by_domain is 'the gain of flipping that domain's misses together', each domain on its own. The file says itself that these values don't add up, because the curve bends and the 580 cap clips. Yet it prints each domain as '% of your gap' and runs a weight check ('48% of the points you lost'). Those only make sense if the domains add to 100%. On the lower route the first flips use up the room below 580, so each domain alone can show a large gain while the true total is small. The shares can then add to well over 100%, and that happens to exactly the students who most need the card. The by-cause and by-tier bars have a related problem: their cumulative order is fixed, so whichever bucket is flipped first gets a different share. That makes 'Traps ≈ 60' partly an artifact of the order.
failures.fix: Split the total gap by Shapley value: average each group's gain over every order of flipping the groups. Four domains means 24 orders × 4 re-scores; five causes means 120 × 5. That is ≤ 600 re-scores of ≤ 44 items, a few ms. Use it for by_domain, by_cause and by_tier, so every share adds exactly to all_right.mid − mid and doesn't depend on order. Keep the per-miss 'worth' as it is. Acceptance: for a lower-route mock at the cap, [.ledger.by_domain[].pts]|add == .ledger.total within 1, and so do by_cause and by_tier.

failures.feature: Review modal body (row 13): their long Justification paragraph plus a Distractor Analysis line per wrong option
failures.why_not_way_better: The WAY BETTER verdict rests on SR16's Steps (P1), SR10 and SR12. P1 is Effort L and 'grows template by template'. Its first milestone is 50% of the test by weight, and templates without steps show 'the Short tab otherwise': the rationale, which the file itself puts at a median of 21 words. SR10 only covers grid-ins (12 of 44). SR12's crowd lines ship empty (see the SR12 failure). So on at least half of the questions a student reviews, our explanation is shorter than theirs. It has per-option misconception lines, which match their Distractor Analysis. That's parity or worse, not way better.
failures.fix: Make P1 steps a launch requirement for every template the section blueprint and the diagnostic can draw. Add a report acceptance check: `tools/steps_coverage.py` reports 100% of section-eligible templates. Until a template has steps, give its explanation card a 'Method' block of at least 3 sentences written for that template (the type's about line, the method, and the check that catches the common trap), above the rationale and the P1 option lines. Never show just the 21-word line.

failures.feature: Question Score 1–7 / Details popover / 'how students do' (rows 17, 18, 13) → SR12 crowd, level, Should-have-had
failures.why_not_way_better: The file admits that no (template, tier) has 20 first tries, so every crowd line ships as 'Not enough students yet · n so far' for months. That empties or disables most of SR12: Should-have-had, Hard for everyone, Colour by Crowd, the option shares, 'L4 · 74% of students get this type right', the hero fact '4 misses are on types most students get right', its takeaway, and the Students-right column. Levels start from P11's tier priors (L2/L4/L6), so on day one Colour by Level is just Easy/Medium/Hard renamed. What ships at launch is no better than their Easy/Medium/Hard plus a Question Score.
failures.fix: Give SR12 a working fallback from P11's ratings, which exist from the first answer. Should-have-had = a miss where your odds E (skill_ratings vs item_ratings) were ≥ 75%. 'Hard for you' = ≤ 35%. The header line reads 'L4 · your odds were 82% · rough (6)'. The average-student line uses a 1000-rated learner's E and is labelled 'estimated'. Use the measured crowd once n ≥ 20. Acceptance: on the shipped db, a sitting with a miss on a type where the learner's odds were ≥ 0.75 shows a non-zero, enabled Should-have-had chip.

failures.feature: Attempt History and Question Overview's Mixed status (rows 19, 20, 32): each try in a practice session shown, and wrong-then-right shown as Mixed
failures.why_not_way_better: We drop something of theirs. A practice set's report never reads S4's `tries` table (session, qid, n, given, correct, reason, ms). The report's status set has no Mixed, although R20 defines it ('right on try 2 or 3 in retry mode'). The player's 'Earlier on this question type' and the SR16 trajectory cover other sittings and draw one glyph for this one. A retry-mode set therefore reports a wrong-then-right question as plain Incorrect and hides the tries. Their Attempt History ('#1 ⊗ Incorrect · Option A · 00:22') and their Mixed cell both show that.
failures.fix: Review items for practice sets gain `tries [{n, given, correct, reason, ms, at}]` and status `mixed`, using R20's ~ diagonal token. Add Mixed to the Show chips, the legend and Colour by Status. In the player, above the type's trajectory, show 'Tries in this set: ✕ A · used the slope as the intercept · 0:22 → ✓ C · 0:41'. Acceptance: a retry-mode drill with one wrong-then-right question has review status 'mixed', a ~ cell, and two try rows in the player.

failures.feature: Per-contest stats (row 30): Score / Correct / Incorrect / Skipped / Voided
failures.why_not_way_better: We drop something of theirs, and two sections disagree. Compete stores right / wrong / skipped / voided and points_parts (base, pace, finish) in sessions.result and shows them on its own panel. The report for a challenge sitting shows only '8/10 · 9:42 · #12 of 140 · average 6.1/10'. Its statuses and Show filter have no Skipped and no contest Voided, and its only buckets are Correct / Incorrect / Unanswered. So the report and Compete's panel give different numbers for the same sitting, and the points the board ranks by never appear. SR19 also uses ⊘ 'Voided' for 'key corrected', which clashes with R20's meaning ('voided by leaving or copying').
failures.fix: For contest kinds, review items carry the skipped and voided statuses (R20 tokens) with Show chips and legend entries. The challenge hero shows 'Points 230 · base 200 · pace 20 · finish 10' and 'right 8 · wrong 1 · skipped 1 · voided 0' from sessions.result. Challenge tiles are Points / Right / Wrong / Skipped / Voided / Time / Per question / Rank. A key correction gets its own state, 'Removed from scoring', with its own glyph, so ⊘ keeps R20's meaning. Acceptance: a daily with one skip and one void shows the same counts and points as GET /api/contest/daily me.result.

failures.feature: Total score card (row 3) → SR4 total from a self-reported R&W score
failures.why_not_way_better: Their total is measured from a real R&W section. Ours adds a number the student typed in (or an outside score) to our Math band. Showing where the number came from doesn't make it more accurate. Calling this WAY BETTER overstates it. By decision 3 this row can't beat a measured total until the R&W bank exists, and the scorecard should say so rather than claim a win. The total also gets no national percentile (SR5 covers Math only) and no split of the gap to the total target.
failures.fix: Change the verdict to 'below theirs until the R&W bank (decision 3), mitigated'. Make the mitigation concrete: add College Board's total-score user percentiles (400–1600 by 10, with source and year) to cb_percentiles.json and show 'Total ≈ 1,130–1,270 · about the Nth–Mth percentile' when R&W is known. Keep R&W entries as dated history and plot them as a hatched line under the chart. Split the gap to the total target into 'Math: what this report can move (path: 4 questions)' and 'R&W: your entered 610'.

failures.feature: Question numbering and deep links used by every shared component (grid, sittingCard chips, player hash, CSV): conflicts with decision 3's 'additive later'
failures.why_not_way_better: It contradicts decision 3 ('no Math-only assumptions baked into shared components'). The single numbering scheme 'M1 Q7' and `#q=m1-7`, review items' `module (1|2|null)`, UI.sittingCard's 'M1 ✕ 1 6 7' chips (shared with Tests and Today), the CSV and the aria-labels all assume one subject. A full SAT sitting has R&W M1/M2 and Math M1/M2, so 'M1 Q7' becomes ambiguous. Deep links that tutors have already shared would break, and every shared component would need rework. Copy like '14 of 22 sends you to the harder Module 2' and the compare line 'SAME 44 QUESTION TYPES' is Math-only. The upgrades add `subject` to the ledger and similar payloads, but not to review items or the address.
failures.fix: Review items carry `subject`. The canonical address is `{subject}-m{module}-{n}`. Labels print 'M1 Q7' while a sitting has one subject and 'Math M1 Q7' / 'R&W M1 Q7' when it has two. The hash parser treats `#q=m1-7` as shorthand for Math. UI.sittingCard groups chips by (subject, module). Route copy reads its numbers from each subject's route_rule, not from constants. Acceptance: `#q=math-m1-7` and `#q=m1-7` open the same question.

failures.feature: Per-module grids and filters (rows 9, 11) → SR15's 17-column table
failures.why_not_way_better: Not buildable as written. SR15 makes the desktop table 17 columns: # · Skill · Difficulty · Level · Format · Time (and budget) · Your answer · Correct · Result · Cause · Worth · Second look · Students right · Changed · Flag · Note · Mistake. It must fit inside max 1120px, with answers that can be inequalities or full sentences and a Mistake text column. The file gives no widths, no overflow rule and no print layout for these columns. Builders will either scroll the page sideways or squeeze the columns until they can't be read.
failures.fix: Specify the table. It scrolls inside its own container, never the page, with # and Skill sticky and an edge shadow when more columns are off-screen. Flag, Changed, Second look, Note and Level are narrow glyph columns with header tooltips. Answers show on one line, with the full text in the row's hover card and the player. Print uses landscape with a first table (#, Skill, Your answer, Correct, Result, Cause, Worth, Mistake) and a second for the rest. Acceptance at 1280 px: document scrollWidth ≤ the viewport, and every column can be reached by keyboard.

failures.feature: Results empty state (row 24) → SR24 live sample report
failures.why_not_way_better: Not safe as written. The sample learner 'sample:report' gets a finished section, a completed second look and later attempts. Nothing leaves it out of the numbers computed across all students: the first-sitting percentile n and histogram (R16, SR5), drill.levels() crowd counts (SR12), P11's item-rating updates and replay (backfill), Compete boards and Climb, and the types-met counts. One fixed student's answers skew every new learner's percentile and item levels, and the skew comes back on every rebuild.
failures.fix: Leave learners whose code starts with `sample:` out of every aggregate across students: estimate.percentile and hist, drill.levels, ratings.py updates and backfill, Compete boards and Climb, U8 counts and admin counts. Give the sample fixed timestamps, so its 'recovered' attempts are dated after the sitting. Acceptance: creating the sample leaves rank.n, crowd.n and every item_ratings row unchanged.
